beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards face down. "Let's see how far the habit actually goes."

beats.prompt: The past: the mirror moment when you two finally called the ledger even.
The present: the parts of the old way of running things you've been cutting loose.
The future: the habit you keep giving into without asking why.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, quiz me on this one then. If the Devil showed up, does that mean something's actually wrong with the partnership?"

options.text: No — it's not a verdict on the partnership, just a nudge to notice the habit.
Yes, the card's telling you to walk away.
The card can't be about a partnership at all.

elaboration: Not purely bad — the Devil isn't calling the relationship itself the problem, it just wants you to notice which specific dependency or habit is doing the holding.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But if the chains are already loose, why does it still feel like I need permission every time?"

options.text: Because loosening them takes actually reaching for it, not just knowing they're loose.
It doesn't — you're imagining the whole thing.
The chains being loose means you've already dealt with it.

elaboration: Freedom here is a responsibility you already hold whether you use it or not — the chain being loose doesn't lift it off for you.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the honest reckoning that started the partnership fair, the old habits you've been cutting away, and the one habit you're only now willing to name."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think the chain was never locked — I just kept putting it back on out of habit. I can actually take it off now. Thanks."
